bill.title: To provide healthy food options in military commissaries, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would require military commissaries to offer healthy food options. The source material provides only the title and no additional text, so the specific requirements, definitions of 'healthy,' implementation timeline, and enforcement mechanisms cannot be determined.

industries.rationale: The bill would affect food procurement and product selection standards for military commissaries, impacting suppliers and food processors.
Military commissaries are retail food outlets, and new healthy-food requirements would change stocking and merchandising practices.
The bill directly concerns military commissary operations, which are part of the defense infrastructure serving service members and their families.

plain.everydayEffect: Nothing has changed yet. The title alone does not say what would change for you, and this tool will not guess. Most bills never become law.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
